data.gender_notes: Gaurinandan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Gauri (goddess of beauty) + Indra (rain god) + Dan (giver of wealth) = Gauri-Nandana, the one who delights Gauri. A name bestowed with the blessings of both the goddess of beauty and the rain god. The name Gaurinandan carries the meaning “Golden Delight” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Gaurinandan usually hope their child will grow to embody golden delight and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Gaurinandan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Golden Delight.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gaurinandan total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Gaurinandan" is rooted in Hindu mythology and culture, reflecting the deep reverence towards the gods and goddesses in the Hindu pantheon. The name represents the union of two powerful deities, Gauri and Indra, and the desire to please and bring joy to the Goddess of Beauty. The use of Sanskrit names in the Hindu culture promotes a connection to the rich heritage and heritages of the religion.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Gaurinandan" carries a deep spiritual significance as it embodies the ideals of devotion, beauty, and prosperity. It is believed that by invoking the names of the gods, one can draw upon their divine energy and blessings. In the case of "Gaurinandan", the name serves as a constant reminder to seek the divine blessings of Gauri, the goddess of beauty, and Indra, the rain god, for inner and outer beauty and prosperity respectively. Additionally, the name also highlights the importance of giving and delivering wealth in the Hindu spiritual tradition, represented by the suffix 'Dan'. This name thus serves as a powerful and inspiring connection to the divine and the spiritual ideals of the Hindu tradition.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Gauri signifies divine radiance and grace, while Nandan symbolizes the one who delights or pleases the divine mother. Thus, Gaurinandan represents one who brings joy and light to the divine mother, embodying the qualities of radiance, grace, and delight.

historical_references.reference: Gaurinandan was a prominent Vaishnava saint and poet, born in the 15th century in Karnataka, South India. He is known for his contributions to the Dvipada, a genre of poetic compositions in the Sanskrit language. Gaurinandan's works emphasized the importance of love and devotion to Lord Krishna.

historical_references.reference: Gaurinandan is also known as 'Gauri Shankar' and 'Gauripuram Govinda'. He was a disciple of the famous saint-philosopher, Shri Madhvacharya.
